seeds: N/A for controller; scientific phases must declare their own
stop_reason: Controller review requires repair: process-lifecycle: Persisted process identity is not bound to a host boot. process_identity records only pid, state, pgid and start_ticks; Master.recover_process and _stop_recovered_group establish ownership using pid, pgid and start_ticks. Linux start_ticks measures time since boot, so after a reboot an unrelated process-group leader can match a stale saved tuple. Recovery would then obtain valid pidfds for that unrelated group and STOP/KILL it. Pidfds stabilize the selected process but do not establish that it belongs to the previous invocation. Repair: durably record the Linux boot ID with the worker identity and compare it before inspecting or signalling saved PIDs. A different boot proves the prior local processes cannot remain alive; archive that record without signalling current processes. Records lacking a boot identity must fail closed or follow an explicitly reviewed migration.; worker-boundary: High — The write-scope check has an inventory blind spot. Master.worker derives touched paths exclusively from changes_since(), whose editable_files() excludes .codex, .agents, other configuration directories, and all data/accounting-master subdirectories except deliverables. The explicit control snapshot covers only four files, while protected_hashes() does not inventory prior master run records. An implementation worker can therefore accidentally create or modify excluded project configuration, or overwrite an earlier response/check record, without appearing in touched or violating the supplied protected hashes. This contradicts the declared document-only write scope and preservation of prior evidence. Repair by separating the preservation inventory from the forbidden-write inventory: snapshot and verify excluded persistent configuration and prior evidence, permit only explicitly identified supervisor-generated changes, and reject newly created forbidden files. Do not rely on the workspace-write sandbox to enforce phase-specific paths. Add regression coverage for an out-of-scope configuration write and mutation of an earlier run record.; worker-boundary: High — Integrity-check failures can be downgraded into review unavailability. In Master.worker's finally block, only merge_hashes() errors are converted to ContinuationVeto. changes_since() calls editable_files(), which raises ValueError for a newly introduced symlink and can raise OSError for unreadable files. These exceptions bypass the integrity-failure record and reach phase_review(), which catches ValueError/OSError as review_unavailable, launches a retry, and eventually records ReviewPending. For example, replacing an ordinary editable document with a symlink during a review produces an integrity-verification exception instead of the required continuation veto. Repair by wrapping the entire post-worker integrity assessment, converting inventory/hash/scope-inspection failures into ContinuationVeto, and preserving the original worker exception plus verification error where recording remains possible. A verification failure must prohibit retry and further scheduling. Add regression coverage for a review that introduces a symlink and for an inventory read failure.; state-refresh: P2 — reload_state silently reuses cached state when a previously existing state.json disappears. __init__ can load accepted phases and run history, but reload_state only replaces self.state when the file exists. If the checkpoint is accidentally removed before reload, validation checks the old in-memory copy and succeeds; a subsequent refresh/save recreates that copy as canonical state. This conceals checkpoint loss and can resurrect outdated acceptance or discard newer history if the instance's snapshot is older. Repair: distinguish a genuinely new controller from one that has observed or committed persisted state. Under the writer lock, veto a missing checkpoint after persistence has been observed; require explicit evidence-preserving recovery instead of silently saving cached state. Preserve normal first-run initialization.; scheduler: Unresolved prohibited deletions can escape the continuation veto through an early repair exit. In execute_phase, outstanding_deletions raises MasterError, which is caught and followed by approve_phase_plan. If that call returns None, execute_phase returns before reaching its final outstanding_deletions check. Master.run can then schedule an independent eligible phase while preserved project files remain deleted. The protection interface covers frozen evidence and controls, not every editable file tracked by outstanding_deletions. Repair: enforce the outstanding-deletion invariant whenever a phase yields back to the scheduler, including failed/blocked replanning and other early returns. Preserve the deletion obligations and stop further phase execution until restoration; allow the current bounded repair path to attempt restoration first.; phase-plan-repair: P1 — Preflight verification runs outside the preservation and attribution window. In Master.execute_phase, check_phase(phase, preflight) executes before creating the phase entry inventory and before any pre-edit preservation or capture_phase_changes call. A checker that accidentally overwrites or deletes an editable manuscript file can therefore alter the baseline subsequently preserved for a new phase. On resume, preflight changes likewise fall outside the recorded work window. check_protection protects frozen evidence, but does not restore or attribute ordinary editable files. Repair: preserve and persist the entry inventory before preflight; wrap preflight in its own preserved before-snapshot and finally-based contribution capture; enforce deletion obligations and pass its changes to subsequent planning and review. Alternatively, enforce and verify a strictly read-only preflight with prior-byte preservation. Add regression coverage for preflight overwrite, deletion and failure after a write.; phase-plan-repair: P2 — Partial-continuation freshness omits declared verification inputs. Master.save_continuation hashes contributed files, the test file and deliverables, but does not include checked['input_hashes']. In contrast, save_pending_review includes those inputs. phase_recovery then labels a continuation 'checked_snapshot_not_acceptance' solely from the incomplete evidence_hashes map. Changing a declared research or other checker input that is neither a contribution nor a deliverable leaves that label unchanged and supplies the next plan with stale checked-snapshot guidance. Repair: include declared check inputs in the continuation fingerprint and compare their current hashes with the values recorded by verification; record changed or missing inputs as requiring recheck. Bind the saved check record as well. Add a regression where only a declared checker input changes between partial work and recovery.; evidence: P18 does not bind every build input. In scripts/check_accounting_proposal.py, the 'all candidate sources pinned' check inventories only .tex, .bib, .sty and .cls files beneath the manuscript directory. An included image, CSV table or TeX input outside that directory can be omitted from source_files. Changing that input then leaves the checker pins unchanged, so proposal_gate can continue reporting readiness for a stale candidate. Repair: capture and validate actual build dependencies, including figures, data and external project inputs; bind their hashes into acceptance. Explicitly identify environment-managed dependencies separately. Add a regression where an omitted included figure or external input changes and readiness closes.
